title: Non-developer has Factory's Droid build a lid-closed keep-awake Mac app in about 3 hours
summary: Wanting agents to keep running overnight with his MacBook lid shut, a non-developer asked Factory's Droid to build a fix. In about three hours it researched, built, tested and debugged an open-source menu-bar app, then made a launch video and thumbnails.
agent_role: Droid did the research, build, tests and bug fixes, and produced the launch video (three.js MacBook, Python-generated music) and thumbnails. The human described the problem, switched the app on to test it and asked for fixes and the video.
outcome: Author reports a first version in 15 minutes and the finished app, video and thumbnails in about 3 hours of Droid time.
what_they_did: The poster, a self-described non-dev, wanted CLI agents to keep working with his MacBook lid closed, which caffeinate does not prevent. He asked Factory's Droid to build a solution and had a first version in 15 minutes. He then turned the app on and asked Droid to find and fix bugs and make a launch video. The result is LidAwake, an MIT-licensed menu-bar app that uses pmset disablesleep, with battery and heat cutoffs and a crash watchdog.
how_it_went: He says Droid did the research, build, tests, every fix, the launch video and three thumbnails in about three hours. The app is published on GitHub with a 12-step manual test plan.
worth_knowing: The app installs a sudoers rule for pmset and a watchdog LaunchAgent. Keeping the Mac awake does not keep it online, and an agent waiting on a permission prompt or usage limit still stalls. The README warns against running it in a bag.
prompt: I'm not a developer. Help me build a small [macOS menu-bar / desktop] app that solves this problem: [describe the problem]. First research why existing options like [existing tool] fall short, and propose a plan. Wait for my approval before changing any system settings or permissions. Build a first version, then write and run tests and fix any bugs you find. Document exactly what the app changes on my machine and how to uninstall it. Finally, draft a short launch video and [number] thumbnails. Show me everything before publishing anything.

curation.rationale: A self-described non-developer had an agent research, build, test and fix a working macOS utility, plus make a launch video and thumbnails. The open-source repo includes a detailed README and test plan.
